children: Hyderabad summit highlights AI, GCCs, commercial acumen and influence as India takes on a larger role in global healthcare leadership

The Healthcare Businesswomen’s Association (HBA) India hosted the third edition of its India Leadership Summit (ILS) 2026 in Hyderabad on 11–12 September, bringing together hundreds of senior and emerging professionals from healthcare, pharmaceuticals, life sciences, CROs and Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

Held under the theme “Command the Shift: Influential Leadership in the Age of AI & Global Capability,” the two-day summit examined how professionals can move beyond functional expertise to become influential enterprise leaders as technology and India’s growing global capabilities reshape healthcare.

The first day featured four masterclasses at Amgen India, covering leadership across matrix organisations, commercial acumen, career reinvention and leading in areas where AI cannot replace human capabilities. The sessions focused on practical skills that professionals can apply in increasingly complex workplaces.

The second day opened with a keynote by Amitabh Dube, Country President and Managing Director, Novartis India, who discussed how leaders can turn uncertainty and change into opportunities. Leaders from organisations including Bristol Myers Squibb, Johnson & Johnson, ZS Associates and Novartis also shared perspectives on reinvention, leadership under pressure and the transition from functional expert to enterprise leader.

Mary Stutts, CEO, Healthcare Businesswomen’s Association, said: “India has become an increasingly important part of HBA’s global growth story as well as that of our corporate partners. It was inspiring to see that momentum come alive at this year’s India Leadership Summit.”

Dr. Deepa Desai, Global Board Director, HBA and Founder & CEO, D Cube Consultancy, said the organisation’s evolution reflects a broader leadership opportunity for India. “We have moved from becoming effective leaders, to claiming a seat at the table, and now to commanding the shift,” she said. “As AI, GCCs and India’s growing global capabilities reshape healthcare and life sciences, our leaders have a unique opportunity to lead global agendas from India.”

HBA India has grown to thousands of members in five years, making it the association’s fastest-growing community globally. With chapters in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad and an expanding presence in Chennai, Pune and New Delhi, the organisation is focused on leadership development, mentoring, networking and building the healthcare talent pipeline.

The summit concluded with “The Ripple Effect,” highlighting how individual leadership decisions can influence teams, organisations and the wider healthcare ecosystem as India’s global role continues to expand.
